subject: Maths
chapter: Chapter 6: We Distribute, Yet Things Multiply
central_question: How does the distributive property explain changes in products, expansions, algebraic identities and fast multiplication methods?
in_scope_units: Distributive property of multiplication over addition and subtraction.
Changes in a product when one or both factors increase or decrease.
Expansion of algebraic expressions and collection of like terms.
Historical note on khanda-gunanam and Brahmagupta.
Fast multiplication by 11, 101, 1001 and related numbers.
Square of a sum and square of a difference using area models.
Product of a sum and difference.
Patterns and applications of the identities.
Chapter exercises involving multiplication grids, expansion and mental methods.
banned_topics: Factorisation of quadratic polynomials as a separate topic.

known_pitfalls.correction: The factor a must multiply every term: a(b+c) = ab+ac.

known_pitfalls.claim: All terms in an expansion can be combined.
known_pitfalls.correction: Only like terms with exactly the same letter part can be combined.

known_pitfalls.claim: Increasing one factor and decreasing the other always leaves the product unchanged.
known_pitfalls.correction: (a+1)(b−1) = ab+b−a−1, so the change depends on a and b.

recommended_example_progression: Use 23×27 and the increase-by-1 questions to introduce distribution.
Derive (a+m)(b+n) = ab+mb+an+mn with the rectangular array.
Use the 65² and 55² area models to derive the square identities.
Use Figure it Out expansion patterns to verify difference-of-powers identities.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Figure it Out sets appear after general expansion and after the special identities, followed by a summary of the distributive identity and its three main special cases.
